behavioral_effects: Each CI job runs the registered Make target for its validator, so validators.json ci_job entries name a job that runs the same command as the local validator
make frontend-test uses bun and vitest coverage, so the frontend-test validator enforces the ratcheted thresholds locally

ci.yml gains permissions, concurrency (cancel-in-progress on PRs only), per-job timeouts, uv and bun caches, tag and workflow_dispatch triggers, and a ci-ok aggregate job that is a signal, not a branch-protection requirement
A repo-root codecov.yml keeps codecov/project and codecov/patch informational and turns on flag carryforward, so the now-live self-hosted instance reports without gating
ruff target-version and ty python-version now match requires-python 3.12; sanitize_numeric uses PEP 695 type parameters and the TypeVar import is gone
compatibility_impact: make frontend-test now requires bun instead of npm and enforces the vitest thresholds; make playwright accepts ARGS. The docker job still runs on main pushes only. Pushes to the dead master and fullstack2 branches no longer trigger CI.
follow_up: Phase 1: compose job, frontend build and format check, dependency audits, preflights-are-host-only exception, dependabot
Open a throwaway PR touching a frontend file and confirm codecov/patch posts as informational and the PR comment renders
limitations: Simplification pass: not run; the diff is workflow and Makefile plumbing with one six-line Python change

This is Phase 0 of the CI/CD coverage plan: it adds no new verified surface, it makes the existing mapping truthful. Phases 1-6 add compose-check, frontend build/format, audits, governance-tool lint and coverage, hygiene, docker matrix and GHCR publish, e2e, and nightly
actionlint was run locally via docker (clean) but is not yet a CI step; that is Phase 3
reason: CI inlined its own copies of the validator commands, so the ci_job claims in validators.json were convention rather than fact, and make frontend-test still called npm without coverage so the registered validator did not enforce the vitest thresholds CI enforces; ci.yml also carried dead branch triggers, no permissions, concurrency, timeouts or caching, and the now-live self-hosted Codecov applies instance-default patch statuses that will go red on any frontend PR at 4 percent coverage. After this change every CI job runs the registered make target, the workflow has hygiene defaults and an aggregate ci-ok signal, and a repo codecov.yml keeps coverage statuses informational until real tests land.
risks: ci-ok is not enforced by branch protection (private repo on GitHub Free, direct-to-main cadence); a red ci-ok on main is a fix-forward signal
codecov.yml is read by the instance from the evaluated commit; a syntax error there would surface as a Codecov-side warning, not a CI failure
rollback: git revert. Nothing outside the repository changes: repository variables and secrets are untouched, and the Codecov instance reads codecov.yml from the commit it evaluates.
security_impact: None. permissions: contents: read is now declared at the top of the workflow, which narrows the default GITHUB_TOKEN; no secret is added, codecov.yml holds no values.
summary: Make the Makefile the single source of validator commands and have CI invoke it, with workflow hygiene and a repo codecov.yml
